items.title: The role of basic psychological need satisfaction in the relationship between exercise and well-being in adolescents: a systematic review
items.venue: Frontiers in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

ai.headline: Exercise may boost teenage wellbeing by helping them feel capable, independent, and connected to others.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 23 studies involving over 10,000 adolescents aged 10–18 across 13 countries. It found that feeling competent, autonomous, and related to others was consistently linked to better wellbeing, with competence satisfaction being the most reliable predictor, especially in competitive sports.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that how exercise makes young people feel about themselves may matter as much as the physical activity itself for mental health.
ai.life_skill: Notice whether an activity makes you feel capable and choose ones that do.
ai.fact: Basic psychological need satisfaction—autonomy, competence, and relatedness—was linked to higher vitality, life satisfaction, positive affect, and flourishing in adolescents.

quiz.question: Which psychological need was the most reliable predictor of wellbeing, especially in competitive sports?
quiz.answer: Competence satisfaction emerged as the most reliable predictor of wellbeing, especially in competitive sports.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were observational, so they cannot prove that exercise causes better wellbeing through these needs, and the only randomised trial found no significant intervention effect.

items.title: Effect of Inspiratory Muscle Training on Blood Pressure and Heart Rate in Normotensive Adults: A Systematic Review.

ai.headline: High-intensity inspiratory muscle training may lower blood pressure in healthy adults, but evidence is limited.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at six studies involving 134 mostly young men with normal blood pressure. It found that six weeks of high-intensity inspiratory muscle training reduced systolic and diastolic blood pressure, while lower-intensity training did not change blood pressure.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests a simple, low-cost breathing exercise might help healthy people maintain healthy blood pressure as a preventive habit.
ai.life_skill: Try slow, resisted breathing exercises only after checking with a qualified health professional that they are suitable for you.
ai.fact: High-intensity inspiratory muscle training is linked to lower blood pressure in normotensive adults in the reviewed studies.

quiz.question: What happened to blood pressure after six weeks of high-intensity inspiratory muscle training in the reviewed studies?
quiz.answer: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure were reduced.

ai.caveat: The evidence is based on a small number of studies with mostly young men, and the authors call for larger trials to confirm the benefits.

items.title: Effectiveness of Peer Education and Support Groups on Maternal Health: A Systematic Review of Antenatal and Postnatal Interventions

ai.headline: Peer support during pregnancy and after birth may help reduce postnatal depression, especially for women at higher risk.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 28 studies of peer education and support groups for pregnant and postpartum women. It found consistent benefits for reducing postpartum depression, particularly in high-risk groups, with telephone- and community-based support appearing especially helpful. Effects on breastfeeding and use of health services were mixed but generally positive when support was culturally tailored.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that informal support from other mothers can be a useful addition to professional care for mental wellbeing around childbirth.
ai.life_skill: If you are pregnant or a new parent, consider joining a local or telephone-based peer support group to share experiences and get practical tips.
ai.fact: Peer support interventions can provide emotional, informational, and practical help during the antenatal and postnatal periods.

quiz.question: What mental-health outcome did peer support consistently help with in the review?
quiz.answer: Peer support consistently showed benefits in reducing postpartum depression, particularly in high-risk groups.

ai.caveat: The included studies varied widely in design and reporting, so the findings are promising rather than definitive proof.

items.title: Mental health outcomes and intervention strategies for first responders exposed to disasters and occupational trauma: a scoping review

ai.headline: First responders face higher mental health risks after trauma, and preparedness, early support, and therapy can help.
ai.summary: A scoping review of 14 studies looked at first responders exposed to traumatic events through disaster work or routine jobs. It found links between trauma exposure and post-traumatic stress, depression, anxiety, burnout and alcohol use, while social support and organisational factors appeared protective. Interventions fell into three groups: preparedness and resilience training, early supportive help such as peer or digital support, and therapy for established symptoms.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how workplace trauma can affect mental health and what kinds of support may help people in high-stress jobs.
ai.life_skill: Notice signs of stress in yourself or others after a difficult event and consider reaching out for peer or professional support early.
ai.fact: Social support, optimism, perceived preparedness and organisational factors were linked to better mental health outcomes for first responders.

quiz.question: What three intervention approaches did the review identify for first responders?
quiz.answer: Psychological preparedness and resilience-based interventions, early supportive approaches such as peer or digital support, and therapeutic interventions for established symptoms.

ai.caveat: It is a scoping review of mostly observational studies, did not assess study quality, and cannot prove causes.

items.title: Regimens of vitamin D supplementation for women during pregnancy.
items.venue: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

ai.headline: Higher-dose vitamin D in pregnancy may make little or no difference to key mother-and-baby health outcomes.
ai.summary: This Cochrane review looked at 25 randomised trials involving 7008 pregnant women across 14 countries. It compared vitamin D doses above 600 IU per day with doses up to 600 IU per day, and found little or no difference in the risk of pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, or low birthweight.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that taking more vitamin D during pregnancy is not clearly linked to better outcomes for common pregnancy complications.
ai.life_skill: Talk to your midwife or doctor before changing any vitamin D supplement dose during pregnancy.
ai.fact: Vitamin D deficiency in pregnancy has been associated with adverse health outcomes such as pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, and low birthweight.

quiz.question: Did higher-dose vitamin D clearly reduce the risk of pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, or low birthweight?
quiz.answer: No, the review found it may make little or no difference to these outcomes.

ai.caveat: The certainty of the evidence was low for most outcomes because of serious risk of bias and imprecision in the results.

items.title: Digital journaling enables privacy-preserving behavioral phenotyping and real-time risk monitoring at scale

ai.headline: Digital journaling may slightly reduce anxiety in young adults, but the benefit is uncertain and not proven.
ai.summary: A randomized trial tested guided and unguided digital journaling against mood checks and a control group in 665 young adults with mild anxiety or depression. Journaling showed small, uncertain reductions in anxiety, but none survived statistical correction, and there was no benefit for depression or daily functioning. Separate exploratory analysis of journal entries found reproducible daily patterns in mood and distress signals.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that app-based journaling might be a low-cost way to track mood, but current evidence does not prove it treats anxiety or depression.
ai.life_skill: Try keeping a short daily journal to notice patterns in your mood and energy over time.
ai.fact: The study found that classifier-derived high-risk signals were more common among younger users, with odds decreasing as age increased.
ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, follow-up data were incomplete, and the anxiety findings did not survive statistical correction.

items.title: Productivity, Climate Risk, Financial Inclusion, and Economic Sustainability among Smallholder Tea Farmers in Kisii County, Kenya: A Systematic Review (2016-2026)

ai.headline: Tea farmers’ economic sustainability depends on efficiency, climate, finance and markets, but bonus effects are unclear.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at studies from 2016 to 2026 on smallholder tea farmers in Kisii County, Kenya. It found that economic sustainability is linked to production efficiency, climate risks, financial inclusion, and market conditions, but there is limited direct evidence on how tea bonus earnings affect household income, savings, investment, or long-term welfare.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how farming livelihoods are shaped by many connected factors, and why more evidence is needed before assuming bonus payments improve household welfare.
ai.life_skill: Notice how several connected factors—such as weather, costs and access to services—can affect your income or work stability.
ai.fact: Mean technical efficiency among Kisii tea farmers was estimated at 0.61, lower than in Nandi (0.69), Kericho (0.74) and Mau (0.77).

quiz.question: What did the review conclude about tea bonus earnings and household welfare?
quiz.answer: There is limited direct evidence linking tea bonus earnings to household income adequacy, savings, investment, or long-term welfare.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, did not conduct a meta-analysis because studies were too different, and its conclusions still need verification against the original studies.

items.title: Inferences of p-values, statistically significant results, and confidence intervals – A systematic review of empirical studies

ai.headline: Many people, including experts, often misunderstand p-values, statistical significance and confidence intervals.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 55 studies involving over 15,000 participants found widespread and persistent errors in interpreting statistical results across students, researchers, clinicians and statisticians. Common mistakes included treating p-values as probabilities of hypotheses and confusing statistical significance with practical importance.
ai.why_it_matters: Misreading statistical results can affect how research is judged and how evidence-based decisions are made in everyday life.
ai.life_skill: Check whether a result’s practical importance is explained alongside its p-value or confidence interval before drawing a conclusion.
ai.fact: Presenting effect estimates with confidence intervals rather than p-values reduced some misinterpretations, but high error rates persisted.

quiz.question: What did the review find about misunderstandings of p-values and confidence intervals?
quiz.answer: They were widespread and persistent across students, researchers, clinicians and statisticians.

ai.caveat: The included studies were mostly cross-sectional surveys, so they show patterns of misunderstanding rather than proving what causes them.

ai.headline: Researchers built an AI that learns to solve visual puzzles by evolving its own rules and symbols.
ai.summary: The study tested an evolutionary computing approach on ARC-AGI-2, a benchmark that measures how well AI can generalise from a few examples. The approach evolved the program, its input parser, and its output projector together, using an object-aware scoring method that rewards partially correct answers.

quiz.answer: They evolved the grid parser, the output projector, and the transforming program together.

items.title: Nutrition as a cross-cutting pillar of lifestyle medicine for frailty prevention and healthy aging in older adults.
items.venue: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging

ai.headline: Good nutrition supports muscle, function and resilience in older adults and works alongside other healthy habits.
ai.summary: The paper reviews how nutrition interacts with the six pillars of lifestyle medicine—physical activity, restorative sleep, stress management, positive social connection, avoidance of risky substances, and nutrition itself—in older adults. It finds that adequate energy, protein and micronutrients support muscle mass, functional capacity and metabolic and cognitive resilience, while poor diet quality and undernutrition are linked to worse sleep, stress physiology and frailty trajectories.
ai.why_it_matters: Eating well can help older adults maintain strength, function and independence as they age.
ai.life_skill: Try to eat enough protein and a variety of nutrients each day to support your muscles and overall health.
ai.fact: Frailty is a dynamic state of diminished physiologic reserve that predicts disability, hospitalisation and mortality in older adults.

quiz.question: What does the review say poor diet quality and undernutrition are linked to in older adults?
quiz.answer: They are linked to worse sleep, stress physiology and frailty trajectories.

ai.caveat: This is a mini-review rather than new experimental evidence, so it summarises existing ideas rather than proving them.

items.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response

ai.headline: Scientists mapped how human genes affect cancer cell survival against 16 chemotherapy drugs.
ai.summary: Researchers tested over 18,000 human genes in HeLa cells to see which ones help cancer cells resist chemotherapy. They found that many drugs, especially TAS-102, trigger a shared survival network involving BCL-2 family proteins and lysosomes, and that combining TAS-102 with a BCL-2 inhibitor reversed resistance in lab and animal cancer models.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how large-scale gene screening can reveal new ways to overcome chemotherapy resistance and improve cancer treatment.
ai.fact: Chemotherapy resistance is often driven by gain-of-function gene events rather than just loss of gene function.

quiz.question: What did combining TAS-102 with a BCL-2 family inhibitor do in cancer models?
quiz.answer: It attenuated the lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance in vitro and in vivo.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer reviewed, and the findings come from cell and animal models rather than proven human treatments.

items.title: The Association between Climate Anxiety and Nature Connectedness: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis

ai.headline: People who feel more connected to nature also tend to report more climate anxiety, according to a review of 50 studies.
ai.summary: The review combined results from fifty studies looking at nature connectedness and climate anxiety. It found a significant positive moderate average link between the two, though the studies measured both concepts in many different ways.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that caring about nature and worrying about climate change often go together, which could help shape future support for climate anxiety.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your feelings about nature relate to your worries about climate change, and talk to a trusted adult or professional if climate anxiety feels overwhelming.
ai.fact: Nature connectedness is a person’s subjective sense of connection with nature and is linked to health and well-being.

quiz.question: What did the meta-analysis find about the link between nature connectedness and climate anxiety?
quiz.answer: It found a significant positive moderate average association between the two.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint that has not yet been peer reviewed, and the studies used many different ways to measure nature connectedness and climate anxiety.

items.title: Pragmatic Research in Healthcare Settings to Improve Diabetes and Obesity Prevention and Care for Our Program

ai.headline: Coaching plus tracking may help people keep off weight they have lost, better than tracking alone.
ai.summary: The study compares a lifestyle coaching programme delivered through a patient portal with a tracking-only programme. Earlier work found that people who tracked their weight, diet and activity and received coaching were better at maintaining recent weight loss than those who only tracked. This new trial will train routine healthcare staff as coaches and measure weight change after 24 months.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how everyday healthcare staff might help people maintain weight loss using tools already available in clinics.
ai.life_skill: Try tracking your weight, food and activity regularly and ask a health professional about coaching support if you want to keep weight off.
ai.fact: People who tracked their weight, diet and physical activity and received coaching maintained recent intentional weight loss better than people who tracked alone.

quiz.question: What did the earlier study find about coaching and tracking for weight maintenance?
quiz.answer: Patients who tracked their weight, diet and physical activity and received coaching had better success maintaining recent intentional weight loss than patients who tracked but did not receive coaching.

ai.caveat: This is a proposed trial with results not yet reported, so the finding about coaching remains from the earlier study rather than proof from this new one.

items.title: Engineering ATP import in yeast uncovers a synthetic route to extend cellular lifespan

ai.headline: Changing how much energy yeast cells have can directly affect how long they live.
ai.summary: Researchers engineered yeast cells to take up ATP from outside the cell. Adding ATP extended lifespan, while removing it shortened it, showing that ATP availability directly regulates cellular aging.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that cellular energy levels are a direct driver of aging, which helps scientists understand how energy state influences longevity.
ai.fact: ATP availability directly regulates cellular aging in yeast.

quiz.question: What happened to yeast lifespan when ATP was added to cells engineered to import it?
quiz.answer: ATP supplementation restored and extended lifespan in those cells.

ai.caveat: The study was done in yeast cells, so the findings may not apply to humans.

items.title: Could an erratic sleep schedule be harming your mental health?

ai.headline: Irregular sleep-wake schedules are linked to worse anxiety, depression and loneliness symptoms.
ai.summary: A large study led by UC San Francisco and UC San Diego looked at people with irregular sleep-wake schedules. It found they may experience more severe symptoms of anxiety, depression and loneliness.
ai.why_it_matters: Sleep regularity could be linked to mental wellbeing, so keeping a steady sleep routine may matter for everyday mood and social connection.
ai.life_skill: Try going to bed and waking up at similar times each day.
ai.fact: Irregular sleep-wake schedules are linked to more severe symptoms of anxiety, depression and loneliness.

quiz.question: What did the large study link irregular sleep-wake schedules to?
quiz.answer: More severe symptoms of anxiety, depression and loneliness.

ai.caveat: Because it is observational, it cannot prove that irregular sleep causes these mental health symptoms.

items.title: Too dry for cacti: extreme droughts could push iconic species to extinction

ai.headline: Extreme droughts could push cactus species to extinction across the Americas.
ai.summary: Researchers analysed cactus habitats across the Americas and found that extreme droughts could cause severe habitat loss, putting iconic species at risk of extinction.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows how climate change may reshape ecosystems and threaten plants people often think are tough enough to survive anything.
ai.life_skill: Notice how local plants cope with dry weather and learn which species are most vulnerable in your area.
ai.fact: Cacti across the Americas face severe habitat loss from extreme droughts.

quiz.question: What threat do extreme droughts pose to cacti across the Americas?
quiz.answer: They could cause severe habitat loss and push some species to extinction.

ai.caveat: The findings come from analysis and modelling rather than direct observation of actual extinctions.

items.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning

ai.headline: AI models can complete most simple video game tasks but still struggle with complex navigation.
ai.summary: Researchers created a test environment using the video game GTA V to evaluate how well AI agents can perceive, reason, and control actions. They found that the best AI model achieved 70.9% accuracy on tasks where instructions were visible, but performance dropped significantly for complex aerial navigation and evasion tasks.
ai.why_it_matters: Understanding where AI succeeds and fails in complex, dynamic environments helps us gauge its readiness for real-world applications like autonomous driving or robotics.
ai.life_skill: Notice that even advanced AI struggles with complex spatial navigation, reminding us to verify automated systems in high-stakes situations.
ai.fact: The best AI configuration tested achieved 70.9% overall accuracy on a benchmark of 103 video game tasks.

quiz.question: Which type of task remained difficult for the AI models despite high overall accuracy?
quiz.answer: Aerial navigation, evasion, and interception tasks remained difficult for the AI models.

ai.caveat: This is a preprint not yet peer-reviewed, and the results are specific to a simulated video game environment rather than the real world.

items.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial

ai.headline: Baseline gut diversity was linked to clinical outcomes in a transplant trial.
ai.summary: This study looked at the gut microbiome in patients receiving two different treatments to prevent graft-versus-host disease after a bone marrow transplant. While gut diversity at the time of engraftment did not predict mortality, the diversity present before treatment was associated with clinical outcomes.
ai.why_it_matters: It suggests that the state of your gut bacteria before a major medical procedure might be relevant to how you recover.
ai.fact: In this trial, baseline microbiome diversity was associated with clinical outcomes, but diversity at engraftment was not.

items.title: Diagnosis and need in ADHD and autism care
authors: Philippe Robaey, Peter Szatmari, Kimberly Courtney

ai.headline: ADHD and autism referrals and diagnoses are rising fast, straining services and revealing unequal access.
ai.summary: This article reviews the rapid rise in ADHD and autism referrals and diagnoses in England and other high-income countries. It describes long waiting lists, unequal access by geography and background, and diagnosis being used as a gateway to support. A commissioned review proposes giving support according to need while keeping diagnosis where necessary.
ai.why_it_matters: It helps explain why more young adults are seeking neurodevelopmental diagnoses and how that shapes access to education, work, and welfare.
ai.life_skill: Ask what support is available based on your needs, not only on whether you have a formal diagnosis.
ai.fact: Self-reported autism among adults in England rose from 0.9% in 2018 to 2.6% in 2025.

ai.summary: Researchers studied how fructose, a sugar in sweetened foods and drinks, affects aggressive ovarian cancer. They found that cancer cells surviving chemotherapy release fructose, which weakens the bonds holding neighbouring tumour cells together and may help the cancer spread. High dietary fructose and statins also showed concerning effects in preclinical experiments.
ai.why_it_matters: It raises the possibility that a common sugar in everyday foods and drinks could influence how cancer spreads, though only in lab experiments so far.
ai.fact: Fructose is a sugar commonly found in sweetened foods and drinks.

ai.summary: The study combined short-term sensorimotor adaptation experiments with long-term complex-task learning. It found that learned motor memories are continually fine-tuned over time, and that retention improves with long-term training.
